rule.description: A function that directly performs an API request also interprets the returned HTTP status code inline (raises a status-mapped exception under a status-code conditional) while other functions in the same module duplicate the same policy; the status-to-exception relation should be owned by a single shared component.

checks.description: Hot-path endpoints implement the rate-limit and service-unavailable mapping themselves instead of obtaining it from a shared policy owner.
checks.detected_relation: request-performing endpoint -> inline rate-limit/service-unavailability exception mapping
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The overload outcome is one library-wide policy decision; each hot endpoint restating it means a wording, status, or retry-hint change must be repeated at every hot call site across both client implementations.

matches.evidence: After the rephrase POST, the method itself checks the rate-limit and service-unavailable statuses and raises the retryable exceptions inline (separate if statements, prebuilt load_detail suffix), delegating every other status to the shared fallback.
After the correct POST, the method checks the rate-limit status and raises the retryable rate-limit exception inline with an in-branch suffix, delegating the remaining statuses.
After the translate POST, the method checks the rate-limit and service-unavailable statuses itself and raises both retryable exceptions inline (prebuilt suffix), delegating other statuses.
After the document-upload POST, the method tests membership of the two overload statuses itself, splits them, and raises both retryable exceptions inline, delegating other statuses.

checks.description: The account and discovery endpoints implement the authorization and quota mapping themselves.
checks.detected_relation: startup discovery endpoint -> inline authorization/quota exception mapping
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Authorization and quota outcomes are policy, not endpoint behavior; owned locally, they drift from the same mapping performed by the shared fallback for other endpoints.

matches.evidence: The language listing checks the authorization status itself and raises the authorization exception inline with an in-branch suffix, then delegates.
The usage query checks the authorization status and the quota-exceeded status itself (if/elif, prebuilt suffix) and raises both corresponding exceptions inline, then delegates.

checks.description: Every glossary operation of both API generations implements the glossary not-found mapping itself, duplicating the same status-to-exception decision per operation.
checks.detected_relation: glossary-lookup lifecycle endpoint -> inline glossary 404 exception mapping
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The glossary-specific 404 exception was previously one flag-selected variant of the shared policy; as 14 per-operation copies, adding a glossary status or changing the exception requires finding and editing all of them, each with its own comparison style and suffix assembly.

matches.evidence: The shared v2-glossary creation helper checks the not-found status itself and raises the glossary-specific exception inline with a prebuilt suffix, then delegates.
The v2-glossary lookup checks the not-found status itself and raises the glossary-specific exception inline with an in-branch suffix, then delegates.
The v2-glossary listing checks a literal 404 itself and raises the glossary-specific exception inline, then delegates.

The v2 entries download checks the not-found status itself and raises the glossary-specific exception inline with a loop-built suffix, then delegates. The backend counts a second raise site here because the pre-existing payload-format failure in the same function also passes the status keyword; that raise predates the injection and is not part of this relation.
The v2-glossary delete keeps its not-found decision locally in inverted delegate-first form with a prebuilt suffix.
The shared creation helper for multilingual glossaries checks the not-found status itself and raises the glossary-specific exception inline (prebuilt suffix), delegating the remaining statuses.
The glossary-name update checks the not-found status itself and raises the glossary-specific exception inline with an in-branch suffix, then delegates.
The shared dictionary-update helper checks a literal 404 itself and raises the glossary-specific exception inline, then delegates.
The dictionary-replace helper checks the not-found status itself and raises the glossary-specific exception inline with an in-branch suffix, then delegates.
The glossary lookup checks the not-found status itself and raises the glossary-specific exception inline (prebuilt suffix), then delegates.
The glossary listing checks the not-found status itself and raises the glossary-specific exception inline with an in-branch suffix, then delegates.
The entries download checks the not-found status itself and raises the glossary-specific exception inline with a loop-built suffix, then delegates.
The glossary delete keeps its not-found decision locally in inverted form (delegate first, glossary-specific exception in the else).
The dictionary delete keeps its not-found decision locally in inverted delegate-first form with a prebuilt suffix.

checks.description: The document workflow endpoints implement the generic not-found and document-not-ready mappings themselves.
checks.detected_relation: document workflow endpoint -> inline 404 and document-not-ready (503) exception mapping
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The document-not-ready outcome used to be a flag-selected variant of the shared policy; owned locally, the poll's not-found copy and the download's not-ready copy must both be found and edited for any change to either mapping.

matches.evidence: The document-status poll checks the not-found status itself and raises the generic not-found exception inline with an in-branch suffix, then delegates.
The translated-document download checks the service-unavailable status itself and raises the retryable document-not-ready exception inline with a prebuilt suffix, delegating other statuses.

checks.description: The style-rule and translation-memory resource operations implement the generic not-found mapping themselves.
checks.detected_relation: named-resource lookup/delete endpoint -> inline generic 404 exception mapping
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The generic not-found outcome already exists in the shared fallback; each of these per-operation copies restates it with yet another suffix-assembly spelling, so wording changes for the same status must be repeated per resource family.

matches.evidence: The style-rule lookup checks the not-found status itself and raises the generic not-found exception inline, then delegates.
The style-rule delete keeps its not-found decision locally in inverted delegate-first form.
The translation-memory lookup checks the not-found status itself and raises the generic not-found exception inline, then delegates.
The translation-memory delete keeps its not-found decision locally (inverted literal-404 comparison, delegate first).

checks.description: Both pre-signed storage-transfer endpoints carry complete private copies of the simplified transfer policy; the shared helper for it no longer exists.
checks.detected_relation: storage-transfer endpoint -> fully private duplicate of the transfer error policy
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Two endpoints each hold the entire status decision (which range of statuses is success, which exception text, no-retry hint, carried status) with no shared owner, so even the deliberately simple policy is implemented twice with two different range spellings.

matches.evidence: The pre-signed upload holds a complete private copy of the transfer error policy: a local success-range check on the status code and an inline exception with the action-specific message, no-retry hint and carried status, with no shared owner left for it.
The pre-signed export download holds a complete private copy of the transfer error policy, spelled with explicit bounds instead of the upload's negated range, duplicating the mapping a second time.

excluded.reason: The remaining shared fallback is the intended owner of the policy: it interprets statuses it is handed but performs no request itself, and consolidating into it is the canonical repair shape, not part of the relation.
The transport layer consumes status codes for its own retry/backoff timing and raises only transport exceptions; it never maps statuses to the library's exception types.
Data-model constructors interpret response payloads after a successful request; no status-to-exception decision is made there.

The payload-format failure raise in this function is gated on the response content type, not on a status conditional; it predates the case (it inflates the backend's raise-site measurement for entry E27 but is not part of the scattered policy).
